newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen rebounding on U.S. CPI.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen rebounding on U.S. CPI.

text.p: --------------------MARKET COMMENT---------------------------- * Toronto stocks were expected to gain at the open after a lower-than-expected U.S. consumer price data. * U.S. bonds rallied after the release of the numbers.
Toronto stocks were expected to rally at the open on Tuesday after unexpectedly tame U.S. inflation data gave bonds an early lift.

"Futures are a little bit higher so we will probably get a bit of a lift," said one trader. "There are other numbers coming out this week that people will key off but this one relieves some initial concerns about a very quick rate rise."

U.S. March consumer prices climbed 0.1 percent. Excluding food and energy, they rose 0.2 percent. Economists had expected a 0.2 percent rise in the all-items and a 0.3 percent increase in the ex-food and energy.
The TSE 300 Composite Index dipped 4.31 points to 5679.33 on Monday, bringing the correction from all-time highs to more than 10 percent.
The dealer said investors will next look to U.S. trade data as a key to the future direction.
* Methanex Corp posted a profit of US$0.27 per share in the first quarter of 1997 versus US$0.08 in the prior-year period.

* Alcan Aluminium Ltd said late Monday it will sue the province of British Columbia for compensation over its cancelled Kemano hydroelectric project after concluding that a negotiated settlement is not possible.
